'''Philip Patrick Power''' (born April 1953<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fischer|first1=Roland C.|last2=Hill|first2=Michael S.|last3=Liptrot|first3=David J.|date=18 April 2018|title=Philip Power at 65: an icon of organometallic chemistry|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/journals/articlecollectionlanding?sercode=cc&themeid=5f0819e2-ee23-4f32-8bb5-35569670ae9a|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-07-02|journal=Dalton Transactions |volume=47 |issue=16 |pages=5529–5532 |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|doi=10.1039/c8dt90058b |pmid=29666856 |language=en}}</ref>) is an American chemist who is a [[Professors in the United States|Distinguished Professor]] of Chemistry at the [[University of California, Davis]]. He has contributed to the synthesis, structure, and physical and chemical characterization of inorganic and [[organometallic]] compounds. His research focuses on low-coordinate main group and transition metal compounds.  Much of this work hinges on the use of sterically crowded [[ligand]]s to stabilize unusual geometries.
[[Image:Ar2Cr2PP.svg|thumb|right|200px|The structure of [CrC<sub>6</sub>H<sub>3</sub>-2,6-(C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>3</sub>-2,6-(<sup>i</sup>Pr)<sub>2</sub>)<sub>2</sub>]<sub>2</sub> prepared by Power et al.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Synthesis of a Stable Compound with Fivefold Bonding Between Two Chromium(I) Centers|first1=Tailuan|last1=Nguyen|first2=Andrew D.|last2=Sutton|first3=Marcin|last3=Brynda|first4=James C.|last4=Fettinger|first5=Gary J.|last5=Long|author6-link=Philip Power|first6=Philip P.|last6=Power|date=2005|doi=10.1126/science.1116789|journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|volume=310|issue=5749|pages=844–847|pmid=16179432|bibcode=2005Sci...310..844N|s2cid=42853922 |doi-access=free}}</ref>]]

==Education==
Philip Power obtained a B.A. from [[Trinity College Dublin]] in 1974 and a Ph.D. from [[University of Sussex]] in 1977 (under [[Michael F. Lappert]]). He was a postdoctoral coworker under [[Richard H. Holm]] at [[Stanford University]] (1978–1980). In 1981 he was appointed to the faculty of UC Davis, where he is Distinguished Professor.

[[File:JARKAP.png|thumb|Structure of the quasi-two-coordinate ferrous dithiolate Fe[SC<sub>6</sub>H<sub>3</sub>-2,6-(C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>2</sub>-2,4,6-(<sup>i</sup>Pr)<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>]<sub>2</sub>.  A weak Fe-C(ipso) bond is indicated by the Fe---C distance of 2.427(1) Å. *Membership of Editorial Advisory Board of Organometallics, Inorganic Chemistry, Dalton Transactions, Canadian Journal of Chemistry, Heteroatom Chemistry, Journal of Organometallic Chemistry, Polyhedron

*Sloan Foundation Fellow, 1985–1989

*Fellow of the [[Royal Society]], 2005<ref>{{Cite web|title=Philip Power {{!}} Royal Society|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/philip-power-12113/|access-date=2020-07-02|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb}}</ref>
*ACS Award in Organometallic Chemistry, 2011
*[[Honorary Doctorate]] of Science, [[University of Bath]], 2016
